title: Hof backup policy
description: The immutable, approved backup policy currently in force for one installation (ADR 0006) - created or replaced only when an apply commits a services.yml carrying a changed backup: section, never per backup run. Both a manual `hofctl backup` and the systemd timer's own scheduled run bind to whichever policy is currently applied (backup-plan-v1's own backupPolicyId) - this is what lets a scheduled run skip fresh interactive approval: the policy itself was already approved when it was applied. Never cross-references another schema file by $id (this repo's own convention); the schedule/destinations/retention shapes are copied from services-v1alpha1.schema.json's own backup object, not $ref'd.

policyId.description: sha256 of ONLY this policy's own actual content - installationId, schedule, destinations, retention, includeRetainedVolumes - canonicalized, via scripts/backup-ids.mjs's canonicalContentId excluding policyId itself AND appliedGeneration/appliedManifestDigest both. Those two are metadata about WHEN this policy was last reconfirmed current, never part of the policy's own identity: an apply that changes something unrelated (bumping the generation and the whole manifest's own digest) while leaving the backup: section byte-identical must re-stamp appliedGeneration/appliedManifestDigest without minting a new policyId, and conversely a genuine change to schedule/destinations/retention/includeRetainedVolumes must mint a new policyId even if, hypothetically, appliedGeneration/appliedManifestDigest happened not to change. Deterministic: re-applying an unchanged backup: section never mints a new policyId, regardless of what else that apply touched.

appliedGeneration.description: The generation of the most recent apply that reconfirmed this policy as current - NOT part of policyId's own identity (see policyId's own description). Updated every time an apply commits, whether or not the backup: section itself actually changed that time.

appliedManifestDigest.description: The services.yml manifestDigest of that same most-recent reconfirming apply - NOT part of policyId's own identity (see policyId's own description). Lets a later backup plan confirm this policy document is still fresh (its own appliedGeneration matches the target's actual current generation), without that freshness check ever perturbing the policy's own identity.

schedule.description: The target's own local time, HH:MM - copied from services-v1alpha1.schema.json's own backup.schedule (same pattern). Hof never converts this to UTC or any other zone.

destinations.description: Copied from services-v1alpha1.schema.json's own backup.destinations (same local/s3 shape as backup-plan-v1's own destinations - copied there too, never $ref'd across files).

retention.description: Copied from services-v1alpha1.schema.json's own backup.retention shape.

includeRetainedVolumes.description: Always true for this policy version - ADR 0006's own fixed platform rule that a backup's consistency set always includes every disabled-but-retained persistent service's own volume, alongside every enabled unit's volume. Kept as an explicit field, not an implicit assumption, so a future policy schema version could vary it without changing this field's own meaning.

destinationName.description: Exactly services-v1alpha1.schema.json's own $defs/name pattern (hyphens only, max 63 chars, no dots) - see backup-plan-v1.schema.json's own identical $def for why.

endpoint.description: Never carries an embedded credential (https://user:pass@host/...) - the secretRef above is the only way this destination's own credential reaches the runner.
